drafts.draft_en:
APPROVE is a decision.
BLOCK is a decision.

"Looks fine to me" in a Slack thread is not.
drafts.video_tip: 6-8s vertical, no music. Three text cards on black: APPROVE (green), BLOCK (red), then a blurry Slack bubble reading 'looks fine to me' that cracks. Or skip video: this one hits hardest as plain text.

drafts.draft_en:
A litmus test for whether your marketing team is really using AI:

Are you only making the same ads faster?
Or shipping 50x more variants than you ever could?

If it's the second, your review process has to scale 50x too. Most teams haven't noticed that part yet.
drafts.video_tip: 15s. Split screen: left a human making 1 ad, right AI spitting out 50 variants in a grid. Then the grid piles up in front of a single reviewer avatar. End card: 'Did your review scale too?'

drafts.angle: Cobra effect applied to AI agents (rides @gregisenberg)
drafts.draft_en:
The cobra effect is coming for AI ad agents.

Reward an agent for CTR and it will find the words that get the click: 'clinically proven', 'guaranteed', 'doctor recommended'.

The metric goes up. So does your legal exposure.

Every agent optimizing for performance needs a second one checking whether it's allowed.
drafts.video_tip: 20s talking head with a quick cutaway: a CTR chart going up while red flags pop onto the ad copy one by one ('unsubstantiated claim', 'missing disclosure'). Close on you: 'Optimize, then verify.'
